hypothesis: A pooled split-conformal interval targeting 90 percent marginal coverage will substantially under-cover a rare high-variance critical slice even under exchangeable sampling, and a deployment increase in that slice will also break the marginal target; slice-conditional or correctly normalized calibration should restore the declared slice target.
claimBoundary: The experiment isolates finite-sample split-conformal coverage under a declared two-slice Gaussian residual process. It demonstrates the distinction between marginal and slice coverage and the effect of a known case-mix shift; it does not establish distribution-free conditional coverage, validate a named model, or show that production slice labels or variance scales are correct.

baselines: pooled split-conformal 90 percent interval on the identical calibration and test draws
pooled 95 percent interval as a global-width sensitivity baseline
controls: equal-noise negative control with the deployment mixture shift preserved
balanced heteroscedastic cell separating rarity from variance mismatch
matched calibration and test draws across all policies within each repeat
